learningObjective: Read precision from the predicted-positive column and recall from the actual-positive row of the same confusion matrix.
mediumRationale: Two semantic tables preserve the matrix structure, remain accessible as data, reflow cleanly on phones, and make the two denominators visible without a chart runtime.

pages.insight: The deck connects threshold movement to ROC coordinates and the underlying true-positive and false-positive counts.
The evaluation summary reinforces that accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 are alternate readings of one error table.
The calibration and out-of-distribution examples show why an aggregate score cannot expose the structure of errors.

deckReview.notes: The deck's classification sequence motivates a concrete matrix with an imbalanced example. The site visual narrows that material to one spatial rule: precision is a column and recall is a row.

agentReview.summary: Recommended semantic matrix views to expose which cells feed each metric. The implementation deliberately narrows the broader three-visual proposal to one denominator comparison.

implementation.accessibility: Both matrices are real tables with column and row headers, explicit counts, and descriptive labels. The caption states the conclusion without relying on color.
